# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 21 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 35 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_021_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 21

**1** Mary said to Jesus: "What are your disciples like?"

**2** He said: "They are like children [шнре коуі] who have settled [хоос] in a field [ахе] that is not theirs [нетнтауе ан].

**3** When the owners [нетнтас] of the field come, they will say, 'Give us back our field.' They will take off their clothes [вст] in front of them in order to give it back to them, and they will return their field to them.

**4** Therefore I say: if the master [хоеіс] of the house knows that the thief [хлоч] is coming, he will stay awake [ротр] before he comes and will not let him dig through [шобе] into his house of his domain [ефт нроче] to carry away [нопт] his goods [схіме].

**5** As for you, be on guard [ротр] against the world [космос]. Gird yourselves [ере] with great strength [хом нноч], lest the robbers [хлоч] find a way [маа] to reach you, for the difficulty [хнке] you expect [шіне] will come.

**6** Let there be among you a person who understands [со уне].

**7** When the grain [карпос] was ripe, he came quickly with his sickle [тоуе] in his hand and reaped it. Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear."

---

**Textual Notes (EMET):**
- *Mary*: Mary Magdalene; appears as a questioner in several Thomas sayings
- *шнре коуі*: little children; the disciples as transient inhabitants of the world
- *бст*: to undress, strip — the children give back everything including their clothes
- *ротр*: to be alert, watchful, agitated
- *шобе*: to dig through (as a thief would dig through a wall)
- *тоуе*: sickle; the harvester image connects to several NT harvest parables
- The saying combines multiple independent traditions: the children in a field, the watchful householder, and the ready reaper
